title: The Wilds and the Garden
subtitle: Don't feel guilty. Every flower once struggled just as you do now.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: You arrived earlier than expected. Pointer and Hissabeth will be happy to know you got here safely.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Oh, FYI, Pointer was the researcher who introduced me to Laplace. You might have met her before in Rayashki. She's occupied with a few important visitors right now. We'll talk to her later.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: As for Hissabeth, you can meet her in person and save me the trouble of an introduction.
She pushes open the door.
Meanwhile, on the other side of the building, Pointer enters through another door.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Our appointment was set for an hour from now. You're a bit early, sir.
Pointer steps aside, motioning for the people hurrying behind her to go in first. She studies the quiet girl, not finding anything particularly unusual.

items.speaker: Mr. Kozlov
items.text: There wasn't much work to do today. And Alia always has everything prepared ahead of anything important. I-It's nothing to worry about.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Please take a seat. Windsong and Hissabeth will join us later.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: If you have any questions, feel free to ask me.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Thank you, ma'am. Please call me Kiperina. I have something to ask you.
Kiperina is the first to speak, surprising Pointer. She adjusts her expression, adding a hint of warmth to her smile.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: That's fine with me, Ms. Kiperina. My name is Pointer. So, what would you like to know?

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: If I take the offer and complete all the required training, what will I get in return? Do you pay in ruble or something equivalent?

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: And I'd also like to know if my family will receive my pay in case anything happens to me.
Pointer looks up and examines the girl once more. She can read the worry in Mr. Kozlov's face, but she still can't quite place the look on hers.
Somewhere between courage and fear. Too fine a line for Pointer to draw.
Plants and machines crowd the limited space, struggling for a balance somewhere between jungle and office floor. It's warmer here than in the hallway outside.
Name Day glances sideways, but Windsong has no intention of speaking.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Hello? Is anyone there?

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: The materials you sent from the Far East Branch have arrived safely.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Everything you asked for on your list is there. But you should check it over as soon as possible.
He scrounges around for a clear spot on the desk and pulls a metal vessel from his pocket,
revealing a little sleeping salamander roused from its slumber by a tap on the head that sends a puff of ash into the air.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Hey. Wake up. You're at work.
Hissabeth emerges from behind the machinery and offers a brisk wave to Windsong.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Windsong? Back from the mine already? Are you going to throw a welcome party for our new colleagues?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: The mine can wait, but I can't. Those materials are top priority.
Now Hissabeth turns her attention to the young man in front of her.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Thanks. You might have heard of me. My name's Hissabeth.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: You've read our proposal, haven't you? It'd save me a lot of trouble if you had. I'll catch you up with Pointer as soon as she's available.
Name Day finds himself staring at the curious little snakes poking out, swearing he saw one flick its tongue.
There's no time to hesitate. He decides to follow proper etiquette—handshake, then introduction.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Name Day, Foundation Investigator for the Far East Branch.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Mind if I ask you a question?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Go on. But this is an office, not an interrogation room.
She looks around with an airy glance and, spotting the extra object on the desk, gives the little salamander a second gentle rap on the head.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Why did you ask me to smuggle in this runium?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Don't get me wrong. I didn't report it. It's just ... it's odd. You didn't ask for much, just a few pieces.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: It is a rare resource, I grant you. But I think you could've gotten this amount with no trouble by submitting an application. All you'd need to do is wait for a few weeks.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Was it really worth the risk?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Yeah, because we don't have a few weeks to spare.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Saving every bit of time we can is vital. It is as precious as this bag of sunflower seeds from a distant land. You don't find them often in these parts.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Here.
She lifts her hand and tosses Hissabeth a small cloth bag.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I've already taken my share. Why not plant some of these in the office?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: It won't take too much effort. If you're lucky, you'll get to see them turn their heads towards the light bulbs.
Hissabeth pulls out exactly what she was hoping for.
Rare arcanum energy, tossed carelessly into the air but caught with practiced ease.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Actually, Mr. Name Day, you're the perfect man for this job. You knew what you were smuggling, you had the perfect excuse to come here, and you were kind enough to help. It was quite the effort to track you down, you know.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: So, how did the trip go? Any trouble?

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: You bet there was. Though I'm still not sure what those bandits were after, the runium or our noisy "arcane item."

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: There's a shortage of supplies everywhere nowadays. People take what they can, whether they need it or not.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Even if they managed to take the cargo, it'd probably just end up in another branch of the Foundation or Laplace.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Anyway, you saved us a lot of time and resources.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Just bear in mind, this runium is not something that you can replace even with Sharpodonties.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Thanks. We'll use it sparingly. Please send my gratitude to Ms. Vila.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: And one more thing.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: What would you say if I asked you to stay?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Don't worry. I won't play the Windsong card. It's only a personal request.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: We could save a lot of time with our procedural work if we had a Foundation Investigator on the team.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: And it could be a great opportunity to earn a reputation. Imagine the prestige if the project ends up a success.
He swallows his words, not intending to explain his reason for being here.
Hissabeth's version works just fine—easy to understand, and not too personal.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Are you making any progress?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: As much as we can, but we don't have a single Sharpodonty to our name, and this runium is the sum total of all the supplies we've received recently.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: They told us we could use all the resources left in Plesetsk, but that amounts to jack all. Thankfully, we still have half a rocket, fuel, and a launch button. Still, to make up for the supply shortage, we need additional manpower.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Oh, but there's some good news: we don't have to worry about finding our astronaut. We already have a perfect candidate.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: We're in dire need of an astronaut.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: There isn't enough time for anyone to finish the full training course. No one would be able to acclimate to a zero-gravity environment in such a short time, not to mention the high pressure and heat.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: But you may be the exception, Ms. Kiperina. Your arcane skill may allow us to work a miracle.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: So, if you take the offer, we'll provide you with a salary and try to get you a permanent position here at Laplace.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Hissabeth is already working on it. She has a contact in the Foundation who can help with the procedures.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Alright then. I have no more questions.
Pointer notes that, despite their thorough explanation, the girl seems no less worried.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: But, just to be clear, I don't think my arcane skill is as useful as you believe. It only makes a little firework show.

items.speaker: Mr. Kozlov
items.text: Heh, she's being modest. You know how children are when they receive a compliment, but I tell you she is more than willing to take your offer. Please give her an opportunity. You'll see how reliable she is!

items.speaker: Mr. Kozlov
items.text: By the way, another little arcanist girl joined our circus recently. Do you think she could stay with you too?

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: That's not really how this works. Not everyone's arcane skill works in the same manner.

items.speaker: Mr. Kozlov
items.text: But she would keep Alia company. Please, madam, Alia is still just a child who plays with dolls.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Mr. Kozlov, stop! I haven't played with dolls in ages!

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: I ... I'm already grown up!
Seeing emotion break through the girl's steady silence at last, Pointer feels she's reached the root of the issue.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: We'll take a look at what she can do. Would you be able to bring her here now?

items.speaker: Mr. Kozlov
items.text: Of ... of course. I'll be right back.
He bolts up and out of the office. In his wake, Kiperina hesitates, shifting in her seat, until at last sitting up straighter.
Pointer's smile fades. There's no need for social niceties in what comes next.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Alright, we're finally alone. Now, how about you tell me what you're actually thinking?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Our biggest issue remains unsolved, but I'm most certain we can resolve it.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: The entire project is a mixed bag right now, but I'd say more good than bad.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: If our little sleepyhead in that pod there can provide what we need, our situation should improve dramatically.
She tips the little vessel, giving the salamander a brief experience of zero gravity.

items.speaker: Han Zhang
items.text: I was dreaming of cutting a tree on the moon.

items.speaker: Han Zhang
items.text: *yawn* You'd better have a good reason to wake me up. I'm not your lackey. We made a deal, that's all. And I'm freaking tired after that trip!

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Yeah, and about that deal? I need something from you, now.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: This little pod of yours. It's electrically insulated, heat-resistant, and highly durable against arcane energy. In short: the perfect aerospace material.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: All I need is to sand off a bit of material from it. Don't worry. Just think of it as dental work.

items.speaker: Han Zhang
items.text: Wait, wait. You haven't paid for that yet.

items.speaker: Han Zhang
items.text: A deal is a deal.
She needs a moment to think but eventually lands on a solution.
She hooks a tiny badge the size of a fingernail onto the salamander's tail.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Here's your ID card. Just to be clear, this is only for an internship. You'll need to actually work to earn yourself a permanent one.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: And don't do anything stupid. I vouched for you, and now both our necks are on the line.

items.speaker: Han Zhang
items.text: Oh, it does look good on me. I knew I belong with Laplace. *sigh* The engineers at the Foundation's East Branch are way too competitive for my liking.

items.speaker: Han Zhang
items.text: So, what else you need? I've brought some records about gunpowder-fueled flight, and a few books on Eastern alchemy. Though, I'm not sure you'd be able to read any of them.
As the little salamander chatters on, she flips over its vessel and inspects it thoroughly before pointing to the square markings on the vessel's base.
The others gather close, unable to resist their curiosity.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: What does this mean?

items.speaker: Han Zhang
items.text: Oh, that? You know, I got this pod from the Panjiayuan Antique Market. It's not a genuine antique, but the craftsmanship is quite excellent.

items.speaker: Han Zhang
items.text: These characters here mean "microwave safe." Funny enough, microwave ovens were not that popular when I got it.

items.speaker: Han Zhang
items.text: Speaking of Panjiayuan, you can't find a flea market as big or as fun anywhere else. If you're ever looking for antiques and collectibles, it should be your first stop.

items.speaker: Han Zhang
items.text: Humph, if you want to go take a look, I might just be nice for once and take you ...
Little salamander notices their eager eyes.
At last, a chance to show off its salesman charm—a moment it's determined to seize.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: No, thanks. Just making sure it doesn't mean "danger, explosive." I already learned that lesson from another escapade with an arcane invention.
She returns the dagger she'd borrowed—who knows when—and slips the vial of metal powder into her desk drawer.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Alright. I've collected enough. You were so busy talking you didn't feel a thing, did you?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Now, back to our visitor in the checkered pattern uniform, have you made a decision?
After a brief pause, the question Name Day asks switches the conversation to an entirely different track.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: What are you going to do with the little astronaut when the project's over?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: I'll submit her application to Laplace once she agrees to join us. It'd be great if you could help with her employment procedures.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: I mean, when are you going to tell her the real consequences of the "Storm"?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Same as always, as soon as she gets a permanent position with Laplace.
Name Day glances at Windsong, thinking she might chime in—offer an explanation, at least. But she only nods.
That's just how it is. That little astronaut, whom they've never even met, will have to learn it too: That pale dome and those cold steel buildings can't protect everyone.
Soon, the rain will wash away all that's familiar to them. Again, and again.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Alright, then I'll stay.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: You mean you really want to stay with the circus?
Kiperina doesn't have a straight answer.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: I ... I meant that I'm willing to do whatever you need, but I don't think I want to do this permanently.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Since you say that you need my arcane skill for this project, I'm happy to help, though I don't really know if I can.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: I think you know why Mr. Kozlov brought you all this way.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: When was the last time you had a proper meal?

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Well, we usually have stews, and sometimes Mr. Kozlov will find us some canned food if we're lucky.
Her rebuttal is soft and utterly unconvincing.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: And you still want to spend the rest of your life in that circus?
A knock breaks the silence. Kiperina uses the moment to lift her head.
By the time she sits back down again, the light that had flickered in her eyes is gone.

items.speaker: Mr. Kozlov
items.text: This is her, the girl I talked about. She doesn't speak much, but I feel that she has a good character.
The girl casts a sweeping look across the room, pausing briefly on Pointer.

items.speaker: Mr. Kozlov
items.text: Don't be shy. You can sit next to Alia.

items.speaker: Mr. Kozlov
items.text: What were you talking about? I hope our Alia didn't cause any trouble, madam.
He steps into the room, noticing immediately that Kiperina is fixated on the parcel in his hands. It's filled with things he and Natalya packed—things they thought the girls might need.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Mr. Kozlov ...

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Will I ever have the chance to return to Utrennyaya?
